summary: For this clay-pot seafood dish, head to Somsak Pu Ob (Charoen Rat), a long-running Bangkok street-food stall at 199–205 Soi Charoen Rat 1 in Khlong San. The MICHELIN Guide describes its specialty as steamed crab or prawns with glass noodles: the noodles take on the seafood juices and peppery, aromatic cooking liquid. This is a specific dinner stop rather than a broad market crawl.
whyGo: Try pu ob woon sen (crab with glass noodles) or goong ob woon sen (prawn with glass noodles) at a specialist stall known for both.
Taste the clay-pot style, where the glass noodles cook with the seafood and absorb its savory juices.
Visit a neighbourhood street-food address recognized by the MICHELIN Guide, with an informal local setting.
bestFor: Seafood lovers who want a focused, hearty Thai-Chinese style dish.
Travellers comfortable with a casual street-side meal and possible waiting.
An evening food stop around Khlong San and Wongwian Yai.
skipIf: You avoid shellfish or need a vegetarian meal; seafood is the core offering.
You need a quiet, spacious or reliably step-free dining environment.
You want a quick meal at a fixed time or prefer air-conditioned dining.
duration: Allow about 45–90 minutes for ordering and eating, with extra time if there is a queue. This is a planning estimate; wait times vary.
cost: MICHELIN lists the restaurant in its ฿฿ price band, but a current menu price was not verified. Seafood prices and crab or prawn portions can vary; bring cash, as the listing says cash only.
hours: The MICHELIN Guide currently lists Tuesday–Sunday, 16:00–21:30, and Monday closed. Confirm close to the visit because street-stall hours can change and holiday hours are unverified.
bestTime: Go near opening on a weekday evening for the best chance of avoiding the later dinner rush. Arrive with flexibility in case a queue forms.
gettingThere: The stall is at 199–205 Soi Charoen Rat 1, Khlong San. MICHELIN identifies BTS Wongwian Yai as a nearby access point; allow time for the final walk and check a live map for the best route from the station on the day.
booking: The MICHELIN listing advises contacting the restaurant directly about booking and gives +66 81 400 0542. Call to confirm current hours and whether it accepts reservations; cash only is listed.
accessibility: The reviewed sources do not confirm step-free access, accessible toilets, seating availability or other access services. The Charoen Rat location is described as a humble street-food stall; contact the venue before travelling if you have specific access needs.
practicalTips: Use the Thai names when ordering: ปูอบวุ้นเส้น (pu ob woon sen) for crab or กุ้งอบวุ้นเส้น (goong ob woon sen) for prawns.
Ask about portion size and current seafood prices before ordering, especially for crab.
Bring cash and allow time for the pot to cook and for a possible wait.
The MICHELIN listing covers the Charoen Rat branch; verify the address if navigation results show another Somsak Pu Ob location.
decemberNotes: No December 2026 holiday schedule or special event was confirmed. December is a busy visitor season in Bangkok; check directly for holiday opening changes and consider arriving early in the evening.
uncertainties: Current dish prices and whether particular crab sizes or roe are available were not confirmed.
Holiday hours, queue length and reservation policy may change; confirm by phone nearer the visit.
Detailed accessibility information was not available in the reviewed sources.
